name: The Strings by InterContinental Tokyo
positioning: InterContinental hotel (officially InterContinental The Strings Tokyo) on floors 26 to 32 of the Shinagawa East One Tower, linked by an internal walkway to Shinagawa Station
best_for: Travelers taking Shinkansen bullet trains to Kyoto, Osaka and beyond
Travelers who want a direct rail link to Narita and Haneda airports
Guests who want Club Lounge access with panoramic Tokyo views

facts.text: The hotel is in Shinagawa, one of Tokyo's leading business districts.
Shinagawa Station provides direct rail access to both Narita and Haneda airports.
Shinagawa Station offers direct Shinkansen bullet train access to Yokohama, Osaka, Kyoto and Kobe.
The hotel occupies floors 26 to 32 of the Shinagawa East One Tower.
The hotel has a vaulted lobby.
Hallways leading to the rooms ring around an open atrium.
Each guest room has a premium bed, a spacious bathroom and a large window with a panoramic view of Tokyo's skyline.
Premium Rooms may include a separate jetted bath with walk-in rain shower.
The Score Dining, on level 26, features daily live music.
Kazane is the hotel's teppanyaki restaurant, where chefs cook behind a massive griddle.
The hotel has a fitness center.

highlights.text: An internal walkway leads directly from the hotel to Shinagawa Station, a major transport hub.
Rooms have large picture windows overlooking Tokyo Bay, Tokyo Tower and Shinagawa Station.
Club InterContinental guests have access to the Maestro Lounge, with private check-in, a welcome drink and panoramic views of Tokyo.
The Strings has its own identity with a light-touch musical theme.
A sampling of uniquely prepared teas is available for free in the minibar.

considerations.text: The hotel does not have a pool.
Light sleepers may hear some light clacking from trains in Shinagawa-view rooms, despite double-glazed windows.
WhataHotel notes the business district location may lack a traditional cultural atmosphere.
